Your riding dashboard: maps, routes, music and messages, all of it working without a connection. A short tour shows what the buttons and gestures do.

The motorcycle button is Where to?: search places, addresses, fuel and cafés, offline. Saved routes and recent places wait in the empty search. From there you also pick a point on the map or draw a roundtrip with a finger.
Import GPX tracks, show them on the map and ride them. Every ride is recorded by itself and kept here too.
Call favourites, recent calls and contacts. If Curveon runs on a tablet that can\'t make calls, install Curveon Companion on your phone: it passes calls, messages and music on to the tablet.
Download offline maps, link your phone, choose language and units, and much more.
Switches between the map alone and the map with music and messages beside it. While the map is full, a number here tells you about unread messages.
Drag and pinch as usual. One thing hides under a finger:
The top one turns the map and shows how it is turned now; tap it for the next way:
Your speed, the speed limit and the clock. The speed turns red above the limit, and a line underneath warns of speed cameras ahead. Hold a finger on any road to see its limit.
The newest message, with Reply (spoken through your headset) and Dismiss; swipe it sideways to hide it. With several music apps, swipe the music card to switch between them.

Plug an OBD2 adapter into the bike\'s diagnostic socket and turn on the engine panel in Settings → Engine. Curveon then talks to the adapter over Bluetooth and shows revs, temperatures and more beside the map.
Pick Fastest, Curvy or Super curvy, and the surface. The small symbols on the trip card:
While riding, the bar at the bottom shows arrival, distance and time left. Tap it for the stops and to save the route.
This tour and a list of every symbol are in Settings → Help whenever you need them.

Start with the motorcycle button at the top of the menu (Where to?). Pick a place there, and Fastest, Curvy and Super curvy appear side by side with time and distance. Add stops along the way, or start somewhere other than here. When it looks right, press GO.

First plan a trip (motorcycle button → pick a place). Then hold a finger on the route line, or choose Adjust route → Edit on map. Drag the start, the destination or a stop to move it. Drag the line itself and the route bends through the point where you let go. A tap on a point gives a menu; Undo takes back the last change, Done keeps it all.

A roundtrip starts in the menu, not on the map: press the motorcycle button (Where to?), then Roundtrip. Now draw the area you want to ride in with one finger, and Curveon builds a loop through it without riding the same road twice. Choose how long it may be, and tarmac or gravel. Another loop gives a new suggestion.

First plan a long trip (motorcycle button → pick a place). Then press the three dots in the bar at the bottom, and drag a finger along the part you want to change. Then pull the part out with a dashed line, just as when editing on the map. Only that part is planned again; the rest of the route stays as it is. Press the button again to go back to dragging points.
Mark the part of the route to change: drag along it, the rest stays
Done: keep the trip as it is

Curveon on the tablet shows the map. Curveon Companion runs quietly on your phone and passes messages, calls and music on over Bluetooth. It is the phone that talks to your intercom, so calls and music are heard in your helmet while the tablet stays on the handlebars. Install the Companion on the phone and pick it in Settings → Phone.

No tablet? Curveon also runs straight on a phone, and is then its own companion: messages, calls and music come from the same phone, and no second one is needed. Choose This device in Settings → Phone.
